drawings.notes: Two graduated segments with their labels written vertically along the ticks: below, A > fA > f^2A > ... > f^{n-j}A > f^{n-j-1}A > ... > f^{n-1}A > f^nA = 0, with a brace under the first steps (A to f^{n-j}A) ending in a short stroke; above, ... f^jA > f^{j-1}A > ... > f^{n-1}A, with a brace under it. The upper labels follow the transcription (f^jA, f^{j-1}A, f^{n-1}A); a fourth label at the right end of the upper segment is overwritten and left out. A small graduated sketch further left on the page (near 'f^2A', around x 0.26-0.31, y 0.71-0.77) is not covered by the mark and is not drawn.

drawings.description: en haut à gauche de l'encadré, un faisceau d'une douzaine de demi-droites issues d'un même point.
drawings.kind: pencil of lines through a point
drawings.notes: Twelve strokes from one point, as on the page: none is prolonged through the point into another, so they are drawn as rays from the same computed point rather than as six full lines; the two going down to the right and the one going to the lower left are heavier, and that one ends in a blot. No label. The triangle of arrows C -F-> C, u, V named in the same note is a relation to be set as text and is not drawn. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the rays and their ends match; the heavy ray to the lower right bends on the page and was drawn straight, 1.7 units off at its middle; it is now drawn bending; a short ray to the lower left drawn before is on the page a small separate tick that does not reach the point, now drawn as such (twelve rays, as the notes say); the other strokes are nearly straight and pass within about 2 units of the common point, drawn as meeting there. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
